column1: # Bug yield per landed item: the stopping signal of docs/agents/finish-line-plan.md §1.1. The reviewer appends one row before landing (worker.md, reviewer brief step 4). kind: rulings | roundtrip | audit | mutation | property | judge | gaps. units: what was processed (rulings, mismatching cards, tests written, mutants run, games). Count a bug whatever found it; put the same counts in the landing commit as a `Yield:` line.

column9: note
reconstructed from commit subjects (reports/finish-line-rulings-pool.md §3), so approximate; 5 batches had no fix

column4: 178 equivalence rules and forms read (164 rules, 12 sentence forms, 2 ignored words), 92 docs' Remaining/deviation passages swept (14 re-read by the review), 68 ruling texts reconciled (45 excluded, 23 exemption differences)

row added by the rulings-P154 review (the landing had none); 141 of the batch's 150 texts cited, 2 exempt, 7 deferred (the face-down Conspiracy draft cards); engine bugs: "If [condition], repeat this process once." after two or more sentences repeated only the last sentence (fixed in the oracle compiler, oracle/patterns/followup_loops.rs; Zimone and Dina, the scheme No Secret Is Hidden from Me), and a damage source selector resolving to several objects had only the first deal damage (resolve.rs DealDamage; Chainer's Torment under Anointed Procession); test errors: 9 CR citations naming a different rule, fixed in review (701.8b for discard, 701.8c for the discarding player's choice, 701.17a for sacrifice, 115.5 for triggered-ability targets, 202.3b for X off the stack, 111.8 and 101.2 not exercised, 508.1c for announcing the attacked planeswalker), plus two misdated CR-history claims in the Souls of the Faultless discrepancy entry corrected; 1 outdated ruling exempted and logged (Souls of the Faultless in Two-Headed Giant), Avatar Aang's airbend ruling noted as not yet investigated, no register entries

column9: first audit area; 64 of the implementer's 65 tests passed first time and the 65th (Mind Bend on Blood Moon) failed only on a display-only bug: text changes dropped the plural "s" from rules_text (CR 612.1), and the review found and fixed that fix's own defect (Islands became "Plainss" when the replacement was Plains); no layers.rs change was needed and every initial failure the implementer hit was the test's own expectation; the review's 1 new test (Humility, Opalescence and Worship in both orders, the 2009 ruling, CR 613.6) and 2 extended scenarios (Colossus Hammer on Vampire Nocturnus; the Plains plural with Island Fish Jasconius) passed first time; test error: Imprisoned in the Moon cited 205.3d for behavior of 205.1a; rulings cited where the scenario is the ruling (Kwende, Mycosynth Lattice, Colossus Hammer x2); 1 provisional register entry kept (star-without-defining-ability-is-zero: no ruling settles it); 4 deliberate engine breaks each failed only their predicted tests (6, 1, 26 and 4 of 66); mutation 45 caught + 2 timeouts of 53 (88.7%), 6 equivalent survivors

mana-value batch (143 of 150 texts cited, 7 deferred: Gallery of Legends, Animate Spell, Push Your Luck, Feeding Grounds and B-I-N-G-O; 0 exempt, 0 uncovered); engine bugs: an X spell was offered as castable under a prohibition no X could lift (Gaddock Teeg's "{X} in their mana costs"; the review replaced the implementer's structural filter rewrite, which also missed parity filters, with trying the values of X against the check the proposal's legality uses, CR 601.3a), a card with an unpayable mandatory additional cost was offered for a free cast (Bankrupt in Blood with one creature, Electrodominance), a cast trigger's "that much damage" read 0 (Imminent Doom: a cast event's amount is the spell's mana value), a card proposed for casting from the graveyard was counted by its own cost reduction (The Capitoline Triad: the preview said {4}, the cast charged {5}), and (found in review) the implementer's choice-time castability check judged targets as a card was chosen, so a spell cast during the same resolution couldn't target one cast before it (Twincast after Lightning Strike: Plargg and Nassari, Etali, Izzet Chemister, The Great Synthesis; six existing tests); test errors: 14 CR citations naming a different rule or one not exercised (fixed), 1 shared ruling's second wording untested (TARDIS Bay, now with the plane in play), 1 pinned fallback without its register entry (default-damage-assignment); the Capitoline Triad mana-ability ruling had been listed as uncovered for a wrong reason (the planner does activate sacrifice-cost mana abilities) and is now tested with Ashnod's Altar; no exemptions, no register entries

no register entries

column4: 64 audit tests (casting.rs, CR 601–602/118; all 105 sampled mutants run, 84.6% caught, 89.4% after the re-run)

column4: 1 user decision (keyword cost reductions on an alternative cost come off after the cost increases, CR 118.9d/601.2f; 21 alternative-cost keywords), 3 register entries (1 decided, 2 provisional), 8 new or rewritten tests and 1 extended; 3 deliberate engine breaks
column9: kw::set_alternative_keyword_cost puts the keyword's increases on the alternative cost and its reduction among the total cost's reductions (CastOption::alt_cost_reduction); buyback and morph face-up keep the bounded modified_keyword_cost; engine bug (pre-existing, fixed by the restructure, pinned by the review): the old keyword reduction was built before X was announced, so Catalyst Stone never reduced an X in a flashback cost (Devil's Play, 107.3a/601.2f); the review split the register entry: the implementer had marked decided both the buyback half (still the user's open question, now provisional keyword-cost-reduction-on-an-additional-cost-within-it) and its own extension that an alternative-keyword reduction also comes off additional costs paid with it (Capsize given flashback with buyback, a commander tax, kicker; now provisional alternative-keyword-cost-reduction-reduces-additional-costs); test errors: the Warbringer 'dash cost includes one generic mana' ruling and 118.7a cited in the dash test but not exercised (no scenario without an increase); review tests: X in a flashback cost (Devil's Play with Lodestone Golem), Trinisphere's floor after the reduction, Henzie's per-commander-cast blitz reduction (its unexercised structure); the 3 engine breaks (the old bounded reading, the reduction after Trinisphere's floor, the reduction applied twice) each failed only their predicted tests

repeatable impulse draw batch (149 of 150 texts cited, 0 exempt, 0 deferred, 0 uncovered; 1 open conflict case for the coordinator: Headliner Scarlett's "Once the turn ends, you can't look at or play the card exiled with Headliner Scarlett that turn. It remains face down in exile, and no one can look at it." (2024-02-02) against CR 406.3's "once a player is allowed to look at a card exiled face down, that player may continue to look at that card until it leaves the exile zone ... even if the instruction allowing the player to do so no longer applies" (in substance in every archived CR since 2016-01-16, reworded 2023-06-16, in force on the ruling's date), left uncited; the engine follows 406.3, pinned by tests/cards/permission_scopes.rs); engine bugs: cards exiled "until" something happens were one batch of events, so "whenever one or more cards are put into exile" triggered once, where Laelia, the Blade Reforged's ruling (2024-06-07) has them exiled one at a time: cascade, discover and the RevealUntil exile form (implementer: Game::one_at_a_time_step, regression test with Bloodbraid Elf, Geological Appraiser and Solstice Revelations), and (found in review) the dig-step forms ("until you exile two nonland cards", "cards with total mana value 4 or greater", "X permanent cards": Improvisation Capstone, Invasion of Alara, Tasha's Hideous Laughter, Dream Harvest, Auspicious Starrix); ruling-backed (the CR is silent), no register entry; each call site was removed in turn and the test failed; misattached rulings: Traveling Minister carries Undead Butler's (implementer, logged), Mount Doom Moria Marauder's (review: cited at origin under Moria Marauder, unlogged until now); test errors (review): 13 tests citing 16 rules they don't exercise (610.3, 611.2b twice, 406.3, 603.4, 608.2h, 608.2c for a choice made on resolution, 701.14b for a fight, the 205.3 heading, 307.1, 608.2b twice, 113.7a, 118.3 twice, 121.3), Ral's coin-flip test checking that no priority decision came up in TestGame::resolve (which never asks for one), Sanar's X check that held for X = 2 and 3 (revealed cards are shuffled back), the rulings' "while the stack is empty" untested in the 38-card table's timing helpers and in Ral's -8 test, Vance's Blasting Cannons' "resolves before the spell" unasserted, Elkin Bottle's "until the beginning of your next upkeep" after the Bottle leaves untested, and Mount Doom's misattached ruling without its record; no exemptions, no register entries

column4: 81 audit tests (triggers.rs, CR 603; 17 of 55 sampled mutants reached when landed, 82.4% caught)
column9: third audit area; the implementer's 74 tests found 3 engine bugs (a 'one or more' leaves-the-battlefield ability its permanent lost because of the event didn't look back, 603.10a; an ability triggering on 'a permanent entering causes a triggered ability to trigger' compared the other ability's whole trigger condition, so 'enters or attacks', 'enters or is put into a graveyard' and 'enters, if' abilities never counted, 603.2/603.6a; 'whenever an opponent gains control of a permanent from you' on a permanent taken at the same time as others was given to the new controller for the others' changes, 603.10d) and raised no register entry; the review found 1 more bug (Teysa Karlov dying with the creatures didn't double a 'one or more creatures die' ability: the batch path counted the 'triggers an additional time' effects after the event, 603.2d/603.10a) and 2 defects in the implementer's own unlanded fix, not counted (a reflexive ability inherited its parent's event kind, so Strict Proctor countered Intrepid Adversary's 'When you pay this cost', 603.12; 'enters from a graveyard' abilities were still missed, the cause matched against the card as it last was in the graveyard), and registered the fix's reading as provisional entry ability-triggered-cause-is-the-event (a 'leaves your graveyard' ability on a reanimation counts; Jailbreak's reflexive 'When that permanent enters' doesn't, a recorded limitation); test errors: the implementer's 4 (tokens named 'Spirit' not 'Spirit Token' in 3 tests, Desecrated Tomb's Relic exiled as a cost, Mesmeric Orb past the upkeep, Intrepid Adversary's extra yes/no) and the review's 1 (Grafted Exoskeleton's unattach ruling cited for one of the five ways it lists; the test now covers four); the review added 7 tests (Strict Proctor with a reflexive ability and with an enters-from-a-graveyard ability, Teysa dying with a one-or-more ability, Switcheroo with Zidane, an ability gained because of the event, Khârn taken with others, Commandeer on Through the Breach) and extended 4; 10 deliberate engine breaks each failed only their predicted tests (31, 1, 4, 4, 1, 5, 2, 1 and 1 of 79), except disabling the later-batch filter (born_later), which failed none of them (Living Death's steps are checked one at a time; the suite's Endless Swarm ruling test pins it and caught mutant 226:56); mutation: 17 of 55 sampled mutants reached when landed, 14 caught (82.4%), 3 equivalent survivors, 38 remaining (one of them, 2169:33, killed by a review test checked with the mutant applied)

Headliner Scarlett's ruling (2024-02-02) "Once the turn ends, you can't look at or play the card exiled with Headliner Scarlett that turn. It remains face down in exile, and no one can look at it." against CR 406.3's continuing look (in every CR since the one effective 2013-02-01; today's words since 2023-06-16, in force on the ruling's date) and every other ruling on a look permission that stops applying (Bane Alley Broker, Colfenor's Plans, Grimoire Thief, Kheru Mind-Eater, Ugin, the Ineffable, The Dragon-Kami Reborn, the hideaway note, Hoarding Broodlord; 2013 to 2024); conclusion: inconsistent (D: the user decides; recommended: set aside its look half, keep citing its play half); investigator plus adversarial skeptic, who re-checked every quote (data/, the 130 archived CRs by script, ormos) and refuted nothing; corrections: the P144 record's 'since the CR of 2016-01-16' (2013-02-01), 'the same words' for the leave-the-game note (similar words), a '406.3b' citation in a permission_grammar.rs comment (406.3; not changed); the ruling stays OPEN and uncited, logged in docs/RULING_DISCREPANCIES.md (inconsistent, open for review) as Fiery Annihilation's was before the user decided; MKM release notes unread (magic.wizards.com and media.wizards.com outside the allowed hosts); no engine or test change

column4: 1 rules question (a returned card's "its" value, graveyard or battlefield; about 20 cards' wordings and rulings surveyed and dated, every source quoted), 5 new tests and 4 re-cited; 3 deliberate engine breaks and a compile of every card before and after
column9: conclusion C, provisional (register returned-card-values-by-wording, replacing returned-card-values-current-on-the-battlefield; 4 questions for the user in the item file): the wording decides once the rulings are dated: Reanimate's (2018) and Cleric Class's (2021) rulings were written for the same "its" and read opposite zones until Wizards' Oracle change of 2022-09-02 made Cleric Class "that creature's" (an inconsistent entry in docs/RULING_DISCREPANCIES.md, confirmed); engine bug (a provisional reading reversed): "its mana value" of a card a target or choice found in a graveyard and put onto the battlefield read the permanent, against Sister Hospitaller's ruling (Sister Hospitaller, Death, Queen's Bay Paladin; oracle/patterns/r608_moved_card_info.rs); compiler fix: Deicide's "If the exiled card is a God card" read the exiled permanent, so a Theros God that wasn't a creature was never searched for (oracle/patterns/conditions_referents.rs; the implementer's report had the two labels the other way round); a compile of every playable card face with the base and the branch pattern files differs in exactly those 4 (and Wonderscape Sage, whose Or of land subtypes comes out in a different order on every run), and each change broken alone fails exactly its own tests; the review added the Deicide test for the ruling's other half (a Copy Enchantment copying Heliod is no God card in exile, so nothing is searched) and noted that Deicide's searched name still comes from the target; no test errors; rulings newly cited 3 (Sister Hospitaller 1, Deicide 2)

effects with no duration: control changes, exchanges, text and characteristic changes (133 of 150 texts cited, 0 exempt, 17 deferred, 0 uncovered; no conflict case); engine bugs: a text change rewrote the colors of mana symbols, so Glamerdye's blue -> red made Paragon of Gathering Mists' {U} cost {R} (implementer: cost and cost-change symbols left alone, CR 107.4, 612.2), and (found in review, by scanning every compiled ability for color names) K'rrik's 'For each {B} in a cost' still became {R}, and 'your devotion to black' was never changed (Erebos still counted black after black -> red, CR 700.5a); test errors: the implementer's 2 (Djinn of Infinite Deceits's one target slot answered as two, Shrewd Negotiation's and Trade the Helm's two slots as one) and the review's 40: 29 tests citing 35 rules they don't exercise (702.119a emerge for converge, 603.10 three times, 608.2b four times, 611.2a/b/c six times, 107.3b, 119.8 and 201.2 twice each, 603.4, 513.1a, 603.7c, 603.10a, 607.2b, 702.10b, 508.4, 701.6b, 702.122d, 106.6, 605.3a, 301.5c, 205.1b, 205.3d, 119.9), 3 'the same player controls both: nothing happens' exchanges that held whichever way (permanent control given first; now until end of turn, failing with the 701.12b check removed), Aura Graft's 'leaves the battlefield' and Ashiok's new-object case untested (the latter would pass if a default declined the card), Postmortem Lunge's independent X untested and its return unverified (2), the Glamerdye ruling's token and spell-copy clauses, Aura Thief's first sentence, the Aura half of the exchange rulings and Kyoshi's 'or less' untested; leftover scripted answers checked for every P196 test (none unintended); 1 not-yet-investigated note (Palladia-Mors's ruling spells it 'Paladia-Mors'); no exemptions, no register entries

mana-value-matters batch, second part (144 of 150 texts cited, 0 exempt, 5 deferred, 1 uncovered: Clown Car's "In an Un- game, if X is actually infinite", which the implementer had exempted, moved in review to docs/rulings-uncovered.tsv, since it describes game behavior only the deferred acorn card Urza's Fun House can bring about); no engine bug: 12 deliberate engine breaks (lifelink gains merged per player and split per recipient, a split card's cost not combined, damage always preventable, opening-hand actions in reverse order, Gemstone Caverns offered to the starting player, APNAP order from P0, a resolving spell's "you" read as its owner, a transformed permanent's mana value 0, a discard into exile not counted as a discard, "your life total becomes" set directly, buyback to the controller's hand) each failed their predicted tests, except the buyback break, which CR 400.3 undoes (the card still goes to its owner's hand); Pyre of Heroes's back-face ruling (2021-02-05, Kaldheim) agrees with CR 712.8e/712.8f, no log entry; test errors (review): 14 tests citing 18 rules they don't exercise (103.8, 305.2 for 305.1, 609.7, 119.7, 603.3b, 406.3 for 406.2, 602.5b twice, 118.3, 101.4, 110.2 twice for 112.2, 608.2b, 608.2c twice, 603.4, 607.1, 406.6), 4 assertions that held whichever way the ruling went (Raging Goblin's own haste for Mutinous Massacre, a Hill Giant that no search from the Bears could find for Vivien on the Hunt, Unbreathing Horde's death for "once per source", Valefor's turn order with one opponent's choice forced), 9 ruling parts untested (Arena's shroud and both-illegal cases, an activated prevention ability and a redirection under Leyline of Punishment, cost reductions after increases on an alternative cost, Commandeer's "an opponent" and "target opponent", Tariff's APNAP order and a player without creatures, a modal back face for Pyre of Heroes, Hollow Marauder's "discarded at the same time" and Valefor's "returned ... simultaneously"), and 1 exemption for a ruling with game behavior; column9: fourth audit area; the implementer's 28 tests found 9 engine bugs, each a phased-out permanent affected by an instruction naming it without targeting it (fight, 701.14b/702.26d; exchange of control, 701.12a/702.26e; damage, 702.26b; a resolving continuous effect that applied once it phased in, 702.26e; removing counters, 702.26d; moving counters, also onto a permanent that can't have counters, 122.5; tap and untap, transform, become a copy, 702.26b/702.26e) and raised provisional entry phased-out-source-still-acts (kept provisional: no ruling, and 702.26b's 'can't affect' and 113.7a's 'can still perform the action' read either way; an Aura or Equipment phased out by itself still made its permanent enchanted or equipped, 702.26i: Dreampod Druid, Kor Duelist) and no defect in the implementer's own fixes; test errors: the implementer's 2 (Graft cited as 702.95a, Soulbond, in 2 tests; Review: the implementer's check after paying a special action reversed every special action whose source had left, also those that don't act on it afterwards (Volrath's Curse or Damping Engine sacrificed to ignore its own effect, CR 116.2d; a regression of the item, not counted), now only turning face up and unlocking a door (special_actions::pay_keeping_source); those two were still offered when only sacrificing the permanent itself could pay (Game::can_pay_cost_keeping_source; completes the second bug's fix). column9: engine bugs (implementer): Bloodbraid Marauder's 'This spell has cascade as long as ...' functioned in every zone (CR 113.6b, 112.1, 702.85a; now the stack only, like a self-granted flash); Attraction, scheme and planar decks were shuffled with the game's randomness and renumbered in seat order (CR 103.3a, 717.2, 101.4e; game 175); the 'Order objects entering the battlefield' decision listed (and by default timestamped) a player's objects in proposal order, an order of ids that follow seats (CR 613.7m; game 405); vanguards and conspiracies got their start-of-game timestamps in the command zone's (seat) order (CR 613.7i, 613.7j, 613.7m). Compiler fix (review, latent, no card's compilation changed: the full unsupported listing is identical): the 'trailing as long as' pattern compiled a card's own grant of another keyword that doesn't function on the battlefield ('This spell has storm as long as ...' on a creature card) or of flash/cascade with another keyword to a battlefield ability that does nothing; now refused; the 'has flash as long as' fallback (statics.rs conditional_flash, reached by no card) still gave every zone, now the stack (CR 113.6e). Test error (review): the supplementary-deck seat test cited CR 400.7, which it doesn't exercise (now 101.4e). Review also: the per-player shuffle stream was unpinned (the game's randomness in APNAP order passed the seat test), new test; the survey's 'no instant or sorcery gives itself any other keyword' corrected (Viral Spawning's flashback, graveyard; Molten Disaster's split second, stack; both already right). Repro games 175 and 405 hold; properties 500 games (implementer): seat, snapshot, rollback, determinism 500/500, replay 498 (games 83 and 469 at the time limit, slow before the item too)

column9: engine bugs (implementer, mana_abilities.rs): a mana ability whose cost doesn't tap or sacrifice its permanent was planned at most once per payment (CR 601.2g, 605.3a; Inspired Ultimatum with Diamond Kaleidoscope's two Prisms, Ashnod's Altar with two creatures for {4}, Skirk Prospector for {R}{R}{R}; counted as found, open, by sweep-nov20 too); the pairwise sacrifice check let a permanent that sacrifices itself for mana also be sacrificed to another source (Blood Pet with Ashnod's Altar offered a {3} spell, then the cast was reversed; CR 118.3, 400.7; now a matching of every planned activation's sacrifices to distinct objects); a planned sacrifice could take the permanent of a later planned activation (Skirk Prospector's 2022-12-08 ruling 'be sure to sacrifice Skirk Prospector last'; Game::mana_keep keeps them out of each activation's choices, and since the review the plan is carried out with activations that take no other object first and consumers whose permanent another cost could take before the rest, Planner::exec_key, so Molt Tender is tapped for mana and then sacrificed). Compiler fixes: 'at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep' compiled as 'the next upkeep' and so fired at an additional upkeep of the same turn (CR 603.7b, 500.9; Paradox Haze; 57 cards, now turn_structure::next_turns_upkeep); the renderer read the next upkeep's trigger as 'the next turn's upkeep', so the round trip couldn't tell them apart (Aang, at the Crossroads and Archangel Avacyn round-trip again). Review: plan_with_filter planned a filter's cost and the rest apart, so Ashnod's Altar paying Celestial Prism's {2} and three Phyrexian Altar activations were planned with three creatures and Yore-Tiller Nephilim's cast reversed (a regression of the item, not counted; the combined plan is now matched); test error: the Molt Tender test pinned {4} as the most two Altars, a Bears and Molt Tender pay ({5}: tapped, then sacrificed). Register: repeatable-mana-abilities-planned-per-activation (policy, decided; narrows the sacrifice choices of an automatic payment; the review added the activation order and the combined check), next-turns-upkeep-is-the-next-turns-first (provisional: the next turn's upkeep skipped, it never triggers; the review quoted 500.11 and 614.10a and pinned a skipped turn as not the next turn, Chronatog), automatic-mana-payment extended. Tiers: verified 19,827 -> 19,835, round-trip 8,901 -> 8,895, compiled 3,348 -> 3,346, no drop. Left (engine-gaps.md): convoked creatures in the planner's sacrifice pools; a cost's own sacrifice parts not kept from its mana's plan (Bone Splinters with Phyrexian Altar and one creature offered and reversed, on origin too; Fling with two since the repeats); taps of other permanents, discards and exiles from hand as mana costs, Squandered Resources never planned; Food Chain planned at one mana per activation
